item.description:

Advanced Energy Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty is a chain-networked micro-silicon electrode using CNT wrapping to induce internal isostatic compressive stress, mimicking Prince Rupert's drop. This prevents cracking without solid electrolyte, enabling 78% capacity retention at 3C and 78.8% after 3000 cycles at 5C in full cells. It significantly advances high-energy, high-power solid-state batteries.

item.title: Fluorination‐Tuned Covalent Organic Framework Interphases for Controllable LiF Content in Dendrite‐Free Lithium Metal Batteries
item.description:

Advanced Energy Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This work pioneers a fluorination-gradient COF artificial SEI strategy to precisely tune LiF content in lithium metal batteries. By controlling fluorine substitution (0F–4F), it reveals how electron-withdrawing F groups enhance LiPF₆ dissociation and oxidation stability (5.4 V), enabling 6000 h dendrite-free cycling and high-rate performance. This establishes COF fluorination as a new design paradigm for safe, high-energy LMBs.
🏷 lithium metal battery · covalent organic framework · LiF-rich SEI · fluorination · dendrite-free

Advanced Energy Materials | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 The novelty lies in using a 3D MIEC garnet scaffold to enable uniform lithium nucleation within its pores, eliminating interfacial instability in “lithium-free” solid-state batteries. This yields 99.95% Coulombic efficiency and stable room-temperature cycling without pressure. The work reframes lithium nucleation as a percolation-governed transport process, guiding next-generation solid-state battery design.

💡 Operando ATR-FUV spectroscopy enables direct probing of cathode/electrolyte interfaces, revealing a chemically driven proton-abstraction pathway forming dehydrogenated EC and VC at ~3.9 V—below electrochemical oxidation onset. This identifies a distinct, voltage-driven yet chemically initiated CEI formation mechanism, providing molecular-level insights for designing stable high-voltage Li-ion batteries.

💡 CTF-Bpy is the first photochargeable covalent organic framework storing electrons reducing enough to drive dark H2 evolution. It achieves the most negative photo-OCP (−0.92 V) for an organic bifunctional material, enabling controlled dark release via discharge or O2 reduction. item.description:

Journal of the American Chemical Society | 🔬 Research Article
💡 Atomically dispersed Ce regulates the interfacial water/proton environment around Fe2 atomic pairs, suppressing the competing 2e– peroxide pathway and enabling the 4e– route. This decouples the activity–stability trade-off, yielding 0.92 V half-wave potential, 1.6% peroxide, 96% current retention over 50,000 s, and 1100 h Zn–air cycling—establishing interfacial pathway regulation as a design strategy for alkaline ORR catalysis.

item.description:

Nature Communications | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 Nanorod high-nickel cathodes (including LiNiO₂) achieve stable cycling up to 4.95 V, unlike microcrystal counterparts. The novelty is that bulk structural reversibility, enabled by the nanorod morphology tolerating H2–H3 interphase lattice mismatch, allows full H3-to-H2 recovery on discharge. This enables high-voltage operation without sacrificing energy density, offering a design principle for durable high-energy lithium-ion batteries.

💡 Fluorine-doped graphene with tailored sp²-C─F bonding enables reversible O₂–H₂O₂ interconversion by tuning OOH* binding. This replaces sluggish 4e⁻ zinc-air chemistry with faster 2e⁻ pathways, yielding durable, high-power batteries. The work establishes a structure-property principle linking fluorine-induced polarization to oxygen-peroxide kinetics, advancing fluorinated carbons for reversible energy storage.

item.description:

💡 This work introduces phosphoric acid-induced cross-linking as a novel strategy to precisely regulate closed pores in starch-derived hard carbon. item.description:

Advanced Functional Materials | ⭐ Review
💡 This Review reframes MOF-derived battery electrodes around how conversion rewrites precursor information into working structures and interfaces, distinguishing retention, reconstruction, erasure, and emergence. Its novelty lies in this material-centered, function-oriented framework linking precursor chemistry to interfacial continuity and reversible reaction, rather than cataloguing products. It matters because it guides predictive design, operando characterization, and practical deployment balancing performance against inactive mass, complexity, and cost.

Small | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This work pioneers particle-level mechanical reinforcement of Ni-rich cathodes, achieving a fivefold crushing-strength increase and reduced stress accumulation, which suppresses fracture during high-voltage cycling. The strategy enables 81% capacity retention over 400 cycles versus 36.5% undoped, establishing mechanics-informed design as a generalizable principle for damage-tolerant high-voltage cathodes.

item.title: Sulfonated‐ TiO 2 Nanorod–Reinforced PEO Composite Solid Electrolytes for High‐Voltage Solid‐State Lithium Metal Batteries
item.description:

ENERGY & ENVIRONMENTAL MATERIALS | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 Sulfonated TiO₂ nanorods actively promote LiTFSI dissociation via Lewis base sites, unlike passive fillers. This raises free Li⁺ from 55.27% to 61.27%, enabling 1.5×10⁻⁴ S cm⁻¹ conductivity, >5 V stability, and 1000 h dendrite-free cycling. The work establishes coupled 1D morphology and surface chemistry as a viable strategy for high-voltage solid-state lithium batteries.

item.title: Chemical-Delithiation-Induced Surface Reconstruction in Layered Oxide Cathodes for High-Performance All-Solid-State Batteries
item.description:
بازسازی سطحی ناشی از حذف شیمیایی لیتیوم در کاتدهای لایهای اکسیدی، تخریب سطح مشترک را حذف و عملکرد باتری تمامحالت را بهبود میدهد.
Journal of the American Chemical Society | 🔬 Research Article
💡 Chemical delithiation with NO2BF4 reconstructs Li-rich layered oxide surfaces into a cation-disordered, fluorine-incorporating subsurface layer, passivating the oxidative interface and eliminating cathode–solid electrolyte degradation. This enables ~300.3 mAh g–1 capacity and 82.3% retention over 1500 cycles in all-solid-state batteries, and the strategy extends to Ni-rich oxides, offering a universal interfacial design route for high-energy ASSBs.
🏷 all-solid-state battery · Li-rich cathode · surface reconstruction · chemical delithiation · interfacial degradation

item.description:

Angewandte Chemie International Edition | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 This work introduces the first sulfonimide-based polymer of intrinsic microporosity (FAS-PIM) and directly compares it with flexible, non-microporous polysulfonimide analogs. Adding succinonitrile drives both architectures toward similar conductivity, thermomechanical properties, and reprocessability, despite differing conduction mechanisms. This establishes convergence between permanently microporous and transiently porous single-ion conducting electrolytes, offering design guidance for next-generation materials.

item.title: Hofmeister‐Regulated Amide‐Protonated Hydrogel Enables Organo‐Interhalogen Conversion‐Type Quasi‐Solid‐State Zn Batteries With Practical Iodine Loadings

💡 This work introduces facet-induced electron-bridge engineering via a Mott–Schottky built-in electric field to enhance LiO₂-mediated kinetics in Li–O₂ batteries. By tailoring electron density and sorption microenvironments, it precisely controls Li₂O₂ nucleation, growth, and decomposition, enabling extended cycle life and reduced overpotential. The strategy offers a general principle for accelerating electron transfer and regulating intermediates through crystal-plane and interfacial engineering.

The result is dendrite suppression, 1400 h cycling stability, and high-capacity retention, offering a generalizable paradigm for advanced composite solid electrolytes.
